business.title: Evolutionary game driven adaptive sliding mode control for high-reliability PMSM Systems with d–q axis cooperative strategy under electrical parameter perturbation
business.desc: Interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) in high-power-density applications face simultaneous perturbation of stator resistance, d- and q-axis inductances and rotor flux linkage due to temperature rise, magnetic saturation and demagnetisation. Existing adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC) schemes treat the d-axis and q-axis current loops independently, leaving cross-axis coupling unaddressed and causing conservative gain selection, chattering and current ripple. We propose an evolutionary game driven adaptive sliding mode control (EG-ASMC) framework that recasts the two current loops as cooperating populations in an evolutionary game. Controller gains evolve online via a replicator dynamic whose fitness function couples tracking error, cross-axis coupling residual and torque smoothness. We prove that the cooperative game admits a unique evolutionary stable strategy coinciding with the Pareto-efficient gain pair, that the closed-loop system reaches the sliding manifold in fixed time with uniformly ultimately bounded tracking under simultaneous parameter perturbation, and that cooperative tuning attenuates chattering by a factor scaling with the cross-axis coupling strength. A finite-time disturbance observer is co-designed with its residual embedded into the game payoff. Monte Carlo simulations under five perturbation scenarios show that EG-ASMC reduces q-axis tracking RMSE by 41.6%, torque ripple by 36.7% and chattering index by 50.9% relative to non-singular fast terminal SMC. Hardware-in-the-loop verification on a 7.5 kW interior PMSM platform confirms real-time feasibility at 10 kHz. The per-cycle computational overhead of the replicator dynamic is approximately 7 microseconds, enabling deployment on cost-constrained embedded processors.
